people.moses.meaning: Moses does not act in Judges. Caleb gets Hebron as Moses had said. The Kenites are the family of his brother-in-law. Judges 18:30 calls the priest Jonathan his grandson in this text.
people.aaron.meaning: Aaron does not act in Judges. Judges 20:28 names him as the grandfather of Phinehas the priest.
people.joshua.relations: Son of Nun. He led Israel in the book of Joshua.
people.joshua.meaning: The book opens after his death. Chapter 2 tells again how he sent the people home and died. The people served the LORD while he and his elders lived. The people born after them did not know the LORD.
people.eleazar.role: Priest, son of Aaron and father of Phinehas
people.eleazar.relations: Son of Aaron. Father of Phinehas.
people.eleazar.meaning: Eleazar does not act in Judges. Judges 20:28 names him as the father of Phinehas the priest.
people.caleb.relations: Son of Jephunneh. Father of Achsah. Othniel is his relative and becomes his son-in-law.
people.caleb.meaning: He offers his daughter Achsah to the man who takes Kiriath Sepher. Othniel takes it and marries her. Caleb gives Achsah the upper and lower springs. He receives Hebron and drives out the three sons of Anak.
people.balak.meaning: Balak does not act in Judges. Jephthah names him in his message to the king of Ammon. He asks whether Balak ever fought against Israel.
people.phinehas.role: Priest who stands before the ark
people.phinehas.meaning: He stands before the ark when Israel asks the LORD about Benjamin. Israel asks whether to go out to battle a third time. The LORD says to go up and promises victory the next day.
people.sihon.role: King of the Amorites at Heshbon
people.sihon.relations: Jephthah names him in his message to the king of Ammon.
people.sihon.meaning: Sihon does not act in Judges. Jephthah tells how Israel asked to pass through his land. Sihon did not trust Israel and fought at Jahaz. Israel won and took the Amorite land.
people.joseph.meaning: Joseph himself does not appear. The house of Joseph attacks Bethel in chapter 1. A man shows them the way in, and they let his family go. They later force the Amorites to work.
people.judah.meaning: Judah himself does not appear. His tribe goes first against the Canaanites, with Simeon’s help. In chapter 15 its men tie up Samson for the Philistines. In chapter 20 the LORD sends Judah first against Benjamin.
people.reuben.meaning: Reuben himself does not appear. Deborah’s song asks why his people sat among the sheepfolds. It says they searched their hearts by their streams.
people.simeon.meaning: Simeon himself does not appear. His tribe goes with Judah to fight the Canaanites. The two tribes then destroy Zephath, and the city is called Hormah.
people.levi.meaning: Judges never names Levi himself. Two Levites appear near the end of the book. One becomes priest for Micah and then for Dan. The other travels with the woman from Bethlehem.
people.benjamin.meaning: Benjamin himself does not appear. His tribe does not drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem. Ehud comes from this tribe. It later shields the men of Gibeah and is nearly wiped out in war.
people.ephraim.meaning: Ephraim himself does not appear. His tribe holds the Jordan for Gideon and kills Oreb and Zeeb. Its men scold Gideon, and he calms them. They threaten Jephthah, and Gilead’s men kill 42,000 of them.
people.manasseh.meaning: Manasseh himself does not appear. His tribe leaves Canaanites in Beth Shean, Megiddo, and other towns. Gideon comes from a poor family in this tribe. Its men answer Gideon’s call against Midian.
people.zebulun.meaning: Zebulun himself does not appear. His tribe sends men with Barak to Mount Tabor. Deborah’s song says they risked their lives. They also answer Gideon’s call, and the judge Elon comes from this tribe.
people.issachar.meaning: Issachar himself does not appear. Deborah’s song says his princes were with Deborah and Barak. The judge Tola is a man of Issachar.
people.dan.meaning: Dan himself does not appear. The Amorites push his tribe into the hill country. Samson comes from a family of Dan. In chapter 18 six hundred men of Dan take Laish and name it Dan.
people.naphtali.meaning: Naphtali himself does not appear. Barak comes from Kedesh in Naphtali and calls its men to fight Sisera. Deborah’s song says they risked their lives. They also follow Gideon against Midian.
people.gad.meaning: Judges does not use Gad’s name. His tribe lived east of the Jordan. Deborah’s song says only that Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan.
people.asher.meaning: Asher himself does not appear. His tribe lives among the Canaanites it did not drive out. Deborah’s song says Asher sat still by the sea. Its men later join Gideon against Midian.
people.othniel.role: Caleb’s relative who takes Debir and judges Israel
people.othniel.meaning: He takes Kiriath Sepher, also called Debir, and marries Achsah. Later the LORD’s Spirit comes on him, and he judges Israel. He defeats Cushan Rishathaim. The land rests forty years until he dies.
people.achsah.role: Caleb’s daughter who asks for springs
people.achsah.meaning: Caleb gives her as wife to Othniel. She gets Othniel to ask her father for a field. Then she asks Caleb for springs of water. He gives her the upper and lower springs.
people.adonibezek.role: Ruler caught by Judah at Bezek
people.adonibezek.relations: Enemy of Judah and Simeon. No family is named.
people.adonibezek.meaning: Judah and Simeon fight him at Bezek, and he runs. They catch him and cut off his thumbs and big toes. He says he did the same to seventy kings. They bring him to Jerusalem, and he dies there.
people.cushan-rishathaim.role: King of Mesopotamia who rules Israel
people.cushan-rishathaim.relations: Enemy of Othniel. No family is named.
people.cushan-rishathaim.meaning: The LORD sells Israel into his hand, and Israel serves him eight years. Israel cries to the LORD. Othniel goes out to war and defeats him.
people.ehud.role: Left-handed man of Benjamin who kills Eglon
people.ehud.meaning: He hides a short sword on his right thigh and brings Israel’s payment to Eglon. Alone with the king, he stabs him and locks the doors. He escapes and leads Israel to the Jordan crossings. They defeat Moab, and the land rests eighty years.
people.eglon.relations: He gathers Ammon and Amalek to fight Israel.
people.eglon.meaning: He takes the city of palm trees and rules Israel eighteen years. Ehud brings him payment and says he has a secret message. Eglon sends his servants out, and Ehud kills him. This man is not the Canaanite town named Eglon.
people.shamgar.role: Man who strikes 600 Philistines with an ox goad
people.shamgar.meaning: He strikes six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and saves Israel. Deborah’s song says the roads were empty in his days. The book says nothing more about him.
people.deborah.relations: Wife of Lappidoth. She calls Barak to lead the army.
people.deborah.meaning: She lives under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel and judges Israel. She gives Barak the LORD’s command and goes with him. She tells him the day to attack. Then she and Barak sing the song in chapter 5.
people.barak.meaning: He will not go to battle unless Deborah goes too. He leads ten thousand men down Mount Tabor and beats Sisera’s army. He chases Sisera and finds him dead in Jael’s tent. He sings the victory song with Deborah.
people.sisera.relations: Captain of the army of Jabin. Jael kills him.
people.sisera.meaning: He brings nine hundred iron chariots to the river Kishon. His army loses, and he runs on foot to Jael’s tent. She gives him milk, covers him, and kills him as he sleeps. In the song his mother waits at the window for him.
people.jabin-judges.role: King of Canaan who reigns in Hazor
people.jabin-judges.relations: Sisera is captain of his army. Heber’s house is at peace with him.
people.jabin-judges.meaning: He has nine hundred iron chariots and crushes Israel for twenty years. He does not appear in the battle himself. After Sisera dies, Israel grows stronger until it destroys him.
people.jael.meaning: She goes out to Sisera and invites him into her tent. She gives him milk and covers him. While he sleeps she drives a tent peg through his head. She shows Barak the body, and the song calls her blessed.
people.heber.meaning: He leaves the other Kenites and sets his tent near Kedesh. His house is at peace with Jabin. So Sisera runs to his wife’s tent. Heber himself does nothing in these chapters.
people.gideon.role: Judge who defeats Midian with 300 men
people.gideon.relations: Son of Joash. Father of Jether, Jotham, and Abimelech. Also called Jerubbaal.
people.gideon.meaning: The LORD’s angel sends him to save Israel from Midian. He pulls down Baal’s altar, asks for signs, and beats Midian with three hundred men. He punishes Succoth and Penuel and kills two kings. He refuses to rule, but his gold ephod becomes a trap for Israel.
people.joash-gideon.relations: Father of Gideon. An Abiezrite who owns the oak at Ophrah.
people.joash-gideon.meaning: He owns an altar of Baal, and Gideon pulls it down. The men of the city want Gideon dead. Joash says Baal should fight for himself if he is a god. Gideon is later buried in Joash’s tomb.
people.oreb.relations: Prince of Midian beside Zeeb. Ephraim’s men kill them both.
people.oreb.meaning: He flees after Gideon’s night attack. Ephraim’s men kill him at the place called Oreb’s rock. They bring his head to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
people.zeeb.relations: Prince of Midian beside Oreb. Ephraim’s men kill them both.
people.zeeb.meaning: He flees after Gideon’s night attack. Ephraim’s men kill him at Zeeb’s wine press. They bring his head to Gideon. Gideon points to the two deaths to calm Ephraim’s anger.
people.zebah.role: King of Midian chased by Gideon
people.zebah.meaning: He and Zalmunna camp at Karkor with about fifteen thousand men. Gideon attacks, and they run, but he catches them. They admit they killed Gideon’s brothers at Tabor. Gideon kills them both.
people.zalmunna.role: King of Midian chased by Gideon
people.zalmunna.meaning: Gideon chases him and Zebah across the Jordan and catches them. Gideon learns they killed his brothers at Tabor. His son Jether will not kill them. The two kings tell Gideon to do it himself, and he does.
people.jether.meaning: Gideon tells him to kill Zebah and Zalmunna. He does not draw his sword. He is afraid because he is still a youth. Gideon kills the kings himself.
people.abimelech-judges.role: Gideon’s son who becomes king at Shechem
people.abimelech-judges.relations: Son of Gideon and his concubine from Shechem. Half brother of Jotham.
people.abimelech-judges.meaning: He hires men with Shechem’s silver and kills his brothers at Ophrah. Shechem makes him king, then turns on him after three years. He destroys Shechem, but a woman at Thebez drops a millstone on his head. He is not the Abimelech of Genesis.
people.jotham-gideon.relations: Youngest son of Gideon. Half brother of Abimelech.
people.jotham-gideon.meaning: He hides when Abimelech kills his brothers. From Mount Gerizim he tells Shechem about trees that pick a thorn bush as king. He warns of fire between Abimelech and Shechem, then flees to Beer. He is not the later king Jotham.
people.gaal.role: Man who turns Shechem against Abimelech
people.gaal.relations: Son of Ebed. He comes to Shechem with his brothers.
people.gaal.meaning: He moves to Shechem, and its men trust him. At a harvest feast he mocks Abimelech and dares him to fight. Abimelech’s men come in the morning and chase him to the gate. Zebul drives him and his brothers out of Shechem.
people.zebul.relations: Abimelech’s officer. He works against Gaal.
people.zebul.meaning: He hears Gaal’s boast and secretly warns Abimelech. He tells Abimelech to hide in the field at night. When Gaal sees men coming, Zebul says they are shadows. Then he dares Gaal to fight and later drives him out.
people.tola.relations: Son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar.
people.tola.meaning: He rises to save Israel after Abimelech. He judges Israel twenty-three years. He lives in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim and is buried there.
people.jair.relations: Father of thirty sons. No parent is named.
people.jair.meaning: He judges Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons ride thirty donkeys and hold thirty towns in Gilead. The towns are called Havvoth Jair. He is buried in Kamon.
people.jephthah.role: Gileadite leader called back from the land of Tob
people.jephthah.meaning: His brothers drive him out, and he lives in Tob. The elders of Gilead bring him back to fight Ammon. He vows to offer whatever comes out of his house, and his daughter comes out. He later fights Ephraim and judges Israel six years.
people.jephthah-daughter.role: Unnamed only child caught by her father’s vow
people.jephthah-daughter.meaning: She comes out to meet her father with tambourines and dances. She tells him to keep his vow. She asks for two months on the mountains with her friends. Her father then does as he vowed, and Israel’s daughters remember her each year.
people.ibzan.relations: Father of thirty sons and thirty daughters.
people.ibzan.meaning: He judges Israel seven years. He sends his thirty daughters to marry outside his clan. He brings in thirty wives from outside for his sons. He is buried at Bethlehem.
people.elon.relations: A man of Zebulun. No family is named.
people.elon.meaning: He judges Israel ten years. He dies and is buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun. The book says nothing more about him.
people.abdon.meaning: He judges Israel eight years. He has forty sons and thirty grandsons who ride seventy donkeys. He is buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim.
people.samson.role: Nazirite strongman who fights the Philistines
people.samson.relations: Son of Manoah and his unnamed wife. He marries a woman of Timnah and later loves Delilah.
people.samson.meaning: He marries a Philistine woman, and a lost bet over a riddle starts a feud. He burns their grain and kills a thousand men with a jawbone. He tells Delilah his hair is the secret, and the Philistines blind him. At their feast he pulls down the house and dies with them.
people.manoah.meaning: He prays for the man of God to come back and teach them. He asks the angel about the child and offers a young goat. When the angel rises in the flame, he fears they will die. He later goes to Timnah with Samson, who is buried in his tomb.
people.samson-mother.role: Unnamed woman told she will bear Samson
people.samson-mother.meaning: The LORD’s angel tells her she will bear a son. He tells her to drink no wine and never cut the boy’s hair. She tells Manoah both times the angel comes. When Manoah fears death, she says the LORD accepted their offering.
people.samson-wife.role: Unnamed Philistine woman Samson marries at Timnah
people.samson-wife.meaning: The wedding guests say they will burn her and her father’s house. She cries to Samson for seven days and gets the riddle’s answer. Her father gives her to another man. After Samson burns the fields, the Philistines burn her and her father.
people.delilah.role: Woman who learns the secret of Samson’s strength
people.delilah.relations: Samson loves her. The Philistine lords pay her to trap him.
people.delilah.meaning: The Philistine lords offer her silver to learn Samson’s secret. She asks him four times, and three times he lies. He tells her at last that his hair has never been cut. She has his head shaved as he sleeps, and the Philistines take him.
people.micah-judges.role: Man of Ephraim with a house of gods
people.micah-judges.relations: Son of an unnamed mother. He hires a young Levite as priest.
people.micah-judges.meaning: He returns silver he took from his mother, and she has an image made. He hires a young Levite as his priest. Men of Dan take his images and his priest, and he cannot stop them. He is not the prophet Micah.
people.jonathan-priest.role: Levite priest for Micah, then for Dan
people.jonathan-priest.relations: Judges 18:30 calls him son of Gershom, son of Moses.
people.jonathan-priest.meaning: A young Levite leaves Bethlehem and becomes Micah’s priest for pay. Men of Dan offer him a whole tribe, and he goes with Micah’s images. Judges 18:30 names Dan’s priest Jonathan, likely this same Levite. Old copies differ over whether his ancestor’s name is Moses or Manasseh.
people.levite-traveler.role: Unnamed Levite whose report starts a war
people.levite-traveler.relations: The text calls the woman from Bethlehem his concubine. He travels with a servant.
people.levite-traveler.meaning: He goes to Bethlehem to bring the woman home. At Gibeah a mob surrounds the house, and he pushes her out to them. He cuts up her body and sends the pieces through Israel. At Mizpah he tells the tribes of the crime but leaves out his own act.
people.levite-concubine.relations: The text calls her the Levite’s concubine. Her father lives in Bethlehem.
people.levite-concubine.meaning: She leaves the Levite and goes to her father’s house for four months. He comes for her, and they stop at Gibeah for the night. The men of the city abuse her all night. She falls at the door, and the text gives her no words.
places.canaan.summary: Israel’s tribes fight for this land in chapter 1. Many Canaanites stay in their towns. Chapter 3 names the peoples the LORD left there to test Israel.
places.canaan.limits: The marker shows a broad region. Its borders are not exact.
places.hebron.summary: Judah fights the Canaanites here in chapter 1. Caleb receives the town and drives out the three sons of Anak. Its older name was Kiriath Arba.
places.hebron.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.heshbon.summary: Jephthah names this town in chapter 11. He says Sihon ruled here and Israel later lived in it.
places.heshbon.limits: The location is a proposal. The marker shows a general area.
places.gilead.summary: Jair’s thirty towns are here in chapter 10. Ammon camps here, and the elders make Jephthah their head in chapter 11. Gilead’s men fight Ephraim in chapter 12.
places.gilead.limits: The marker shows a broad region beyond the Jordan. Its borders are not exact.
places.gerizim.summary: Jotham stands on top of this mountain in chapter 9. He calls out his story of the trees to the men of Shechem.
places.gerizim.limits: The marker shows the mountain. The spot where Jotham stood is unknown.
places.jordan.summary: Ehud’s men hold the river crossings against Moab in chapter 3. Ephraim holds them against Midian in chapter 7. Gilead’s men kill fleeing Ephraimites there in chapter 12.
places.jordan.limits: The marker shows a crossing area. The text does not say which crossings were used.
places.gilgal.summary: The LORD’s angel comes up from Gilgal to Bochim in chapter 2. Ehud turns back at the stone idols by Gilgal in chapter 3.
places.jericho.summary: Chapter 3 says Eglon took the city of palm trees. Judges itself does not use the name Jericho.
places.jericho.limits: Judges does not say the city of palm trees is Jericho. The marker follows a traditional identification.
places.bethel.summary: The house of Joseph takes this town in chapter 1. Its older name was Luz. In chapters 20 and 21 Israel comes here to ask God and to weep.
places.bethel.limits: The marker follows a traditional identification of the town.
places.jerusalem.summary: Judah takes the city and burns it in chapter 1. Benjamin does not drive out the Jebusites. In chapter 19 the Levite will not stay in this foreign city, called Jebus.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.hazor.summary: Jabin king of Canaan reigns here in chapter 4. His captain Sisera lives in another town, Harosheth of the Gentiles.
places.hazor.limits: The marker shows the site’s general location.
places.debir-town.summary: Othniel takes this town in chapter 1 and wins Achsah as his wife. Its older name was Kiriath Sepher.
places.debir-town.limits: The location is approximate. The marker shows a southern region, not a known site.
places.shiloh.summary: In chapter 21 Israel brings four hundred young women to the camp here. Men of Benjamin then seize wives from the dancers at Shiloh’s yearly feast.
places.shiloh.limits: The marker follows a traditional identification. Judges 21:19 places Shiloh north of Bethel.
places.shechem.summary: Abimelech’s mother’s family lives here, and the town makes him king in chapter 9. Gaal turns the town against him. Abimelech destroys it and sows it with salt.
places.shechem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.moab.summary: Eglon king of Moab rules Israel eighteen years in chapter 3. Ehud kills him, and Israel defeats Moab at the Jordan.
places.moab.limits: The marker shows a broad region. Its borders are not exact.
places.ammon.summary: The children of Ammon trouble Israel for eighteen years in chapter 10. Their king claims Israel’s land in chapter 11. Jephthah defeats them.
places.ammon.limits: The marker shows a broad region. No exact border is drawn.
places.tabor.summary: Barak gathers ten thousand men here in chapter 4. He charges down the mountain against Sisera. Chapter 8 says Gideon’s brothers were killed at Tabor.
places.tabor.limits: The marker shows the mountain. The exact battle ground is unknown.
places.kishon.summary: Sisera brings his chariots to this river in chapter 4. Deborah’s song in chapter 5 says the river swept the enemy away.
places.kishon.limits: The old riverbed and the battle ground are not known exactly.
places.megiddo.summary: Manasseh does not drive out its people in chapter 1. Deborah’s song says the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo.
places.megiddo.limits: The marker shows the town site. The battle ground by the waters is unknown.
places.ophrah.summary: The LORD’s angel meets Gideon under the oak here in chapter 6. Gideon builds an altar and pulls down Baal’s altar. In chapter 8 he keeps his ephod here and is buried here.
places.ophrah.limits: The location of Gideon’s Ophrah is uncertain. The marker shows a general area.
places.jezreel.summary: Midian, Amalek, and the children of the east camp in this valley in chapter 6. Gideon attacks their camp in chapter 7.
places.jezreel.limits: The marker shows the valley. Gideon’s exact camp is unknown.
places.succoth.summary: Gideon asks its men for bread in chapter 8, and they refuse. He comes back and punishes its elders with thorns.
places.succoth.limits: The site is a proposal. Its location remains uncertain.
places.penuel.summary: Its men refuse Gideon bread in chapter 8. He returns, breaks down its tower, and kills the men of the city.
places.penuel.limits: The site is a proposal. The marker shows a general area.
places.thebez.summary: Abimelech takes this town in chapter 9. Its people flee to a strong tower. A woman drops a millstone from it and breaks his skull.
places.thebez.limits: The marker follows a traditional identification.
places.zorah.summary: Manoah lives here, and Samson is born to him in chapter 13. Samson is buried between Zorah and Eshtaol. Dan’s spies and six hundred men set out from here in chapter 18.
places.zorah.limits: The marker follows a traditional identification.
places.eshtaol.summary: The LORD’s Spirit first moves Samson between Zorah and Eshtaol in chapter 13. Men of Dan set out from here in chapter 18.
places.timnah.summary: Samson sees a Philistine woman here in chapter 14 and marries her. He kills a lion near its vineyards. In chapter 15 the Philistines burn her and her father.
places.timnah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site.
places.ashkelon.summary: Judah takes it in chapter 1. In chapter 14 Samson kills thirty men here to pay his bet.
places.ashkelon.limits: The marker shows the old city’s general location.
places.lehi.summary: The Philistines camp here in chapter 15. Men of Judah bring Samson tied up. He breaks the ropes and kills a thousand men with a jawbone. God then opens a spring for him.
places.lehi.limits: The exact place is uncertain. No link to the Book of Mormon Lehi is established.
places.gaza.summary: Samson carries off the city gate in chapter 16. Later the Philistines blind him and make him grind in the prison here. He pulls down their house at a feast for Dagon.
places.gaza.limits: The marker shows the old city’s general location.
places.sorek.summary: Delilah lives in this valley in chapter 16, and Samson loves her. The Philistine lords come up to her here.
places.sorek.limits: The marker shows the valley. No exact spot is named.
places.ephraim-region.summary: Micah’s house is in this hill country in chapters 17 and 18. The Levite of chapter 19 lives on its far side. Ehud and Gideon call men from these hills earlier in the book.
places.ephraim-region.limits: The marker shows a broad hill region. No one knows where Micah’s house stood.
places.bethlehem.summary: The young Levite leaves this town in chapter 17. The woman of chapter 19 comes from here. The Levite fetches her from her father’s house.
places.bethlehem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.dan-city.summary: Five spies of Dan find Laish quiet and safe in chapter 18. Six hundred men of Dan kill its people and burn it. They rebuild it, name it Dan, and set up Micah’s image.
places.dan-city.limits: The marker shows the site’s general location.
places.gibeah.summary: The Levite and the woman stay here in chapter 19. Men of the town abuse her through the night. In chapter 20 Israel attacks Gibeah and takes it by ambush.
places.mizpah.summary: All Israel gathers here before the LORD in chapter 20. The Levite tells what happened at Gibeah. The men swear not to give their daughters to Benjamin.
places.mizpah.limits: The marker follows a traditional identification. Jephthah’s Mizpah of Gilead in chapter 11 is a different place.
places.rimmon-rock.summary: Six hundred men of Benjamin flee here in chapter 20 and stay four months. In chapter 21 Israel sends them an offer of peace.
places.jabesh-gilead.summary: No one from this town comes to Mizpah. In chapter 21 Israel kills its people but spares four hundred young women. They are given to Benjamin as wives.
places.jabesh-gilead.limits: More than one site has been proposed. The marker shows a general area.
sources.web.limits: The text supplies the events and named people. It cannot confirm dates or each historical claim.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Coordinates are display estimates. A town marker does not confirm an event at that town.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or towns.
sources.atlas-exodus.limits: The route shown is a study tradition. It does not prove a sea crossing or a Sinai site.
sources.yale-13.summary: Hayes studies local leaders and the repeated crisis pattern. She also covers competing views of kingship and the violence of the closing chapters.
sources.yale-13.limits: The reviewed section is a 2006 lecture interpretation. This guide did not check its proposed source layers and dates.
sources.sbl-gender.summary: The volume studies gender and social position in Judges. It also studies how links to other biblical texts shape readings.
sources.net-judges-18.summary: The translators compare the Moses and Manasseh readings in Jonathan’s family line. They prefer Moses. They discuss a suspended letter in Hebrew manuscripts.
sources.net-judges-18.limits: The published textual note was reviewed. Its account of the scribes’ purpose is an editorial judgment. This guide did not review the manuscripts in full.
sources.cfm-2026-22.limits: This is Church teaching and application. It does not supply archaeological evidence or event dates.
sources.wiki-judges.limits: Anyone can edit this source. Use it for background and to find other sources. Its disputed history claims need separate scholarly review.
sources.dm-judges.limits: This is one scholar’s older interpretation. It makes a speculative link between Sisera’s name and Ramses II. This guide leaves that link out and takes no event date from it.
chapters.*.mapNote: The points show the towns and regions the chapter names. Many locations are approximate.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The line follows the movement the chapter names. The real roads between the points are unknown.
